lockFileMaintenance.description: Label the weekly whole-tree refresh so it is distinguishable from a targeted update. The release-age hold is nulled here: regeneration lets npm and cargo pick transitive versions, so the hold cannot be enforced and would sit pending on nearly every run. Green required checks automerge the refresh; a red one stays open for diagnosis.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: minimumReleaseAge restates Renovate's own default for this block; without it the 3-day hold above reads as applying to security fixes.

packageRules.description: Update lockfiles within compatible cargo and npm ranges; replace ranges for incompatible releases.

Do not manage the npm overrides block as first-class dependencies. Its entries are deliberate transitive security floors, and because the packages are transitive-only, a per-entry lockfile bump runs npm install <pkg>@<version>, which npm rejects with EOVERRIDE. That failure blocked the hono lockfile branch and the npm side of lock file maintenance. Pinned transitive versions still refresh within range through normal lockfile updates.
Hold major upgrades for dashboard approval and process them after lower-risk updates.
Pin Docker base images by digest for reproducible, tamper-evident builds.
Automerge patch, pin, and digest updates for Docker Official Images after required checks pass.
Treat GitHub-owned actions as platform dependencies and automerge patch, pin, and digest updates after required checks pass.
Automerge third-party action patch and pin updates; require manual review when a pinned tag moves to a new digest.

Exempt action digest updates from the release-age hold. The hold earns its keep against a newly published version that has not been in the wild long enough to be trusted. A digest update is not that: it re-pins an action to the commit its already-pinned major tag now names, which is the version this repo has been trusting by tag all along. Holding it only means carrying a knowingly stale pin for three days and occupying a prConcurrentLimit slot while it waits.
Automerge stable cargo and npm patch updates; keep pre-1.0 updates manual.
Group compatible React packages.
Group compatible Tailwind CSS packages.
Group compatible TanStack Query packages.
Group compatible commitlint packages.

Keep every PostgreSQL image pin in one PR. scripts/compose-dev-invariants.sh requires docker/compose.dev.yml and the ci.yml backend service to pin the identical postgres digest, so a split across the docker-compose and github-actions managers fails the dev/CI parity gate on both branches. Grouping the CI workflow service with the compose images moves them together.
Keep the SQLx library and migration CLI compatible.
Group compatible Astro documentation packages.
Ignore rand_core_06 because the alias intentionally targets the 0.6 API.
Keep vite-plus and vitest in lockstep: vite-plus bundles the @vitest/* family with an exact vitest peer dependency, so a standalone vitest or vite-plus bump fails lockfile resolution.

The generated color primitives pin these exactly; any bump fails the radix-gen drift test until npm run primitives:gen is rerun and the palette diff reviewed, so move them as one deliberate, dashboard-approved group.

Keep the two npm pins in one PR. scripts/npm-pin-drift.sh requires mise.toml and package.json's devEngines to name the identical npm version, and the two live behind different managers: mise sees the mise.toml entry, and the custom manager below is the only thing that sees devEngines at all. Ungrouped, the mise bump lands alone and every npm release becomes a red PR that cannot go green without a hand edit.

customManagers.description: Track devEngines.packageManager.version. Renovate's npm manager reads only the top-level packageManager field, never devEngines, so this copy is invisible to every built-in manager. Without it the mise manager raises an npm bump against mise.toml alone and reinstates the mismatch npm-pin-drift exists to catch; the npm-pin group above then moves both copies together.
Track SQLX_CLI_VERSION because it is not embedded in an install-action tool list.
Track checksum-verified lint tools; version bumps require the corresponding checksum to be updated manually.

Track annotated version pins in workflows (TruffleHog's image tag, mise itself, and the remaining install-pinned-tool binaries). When a sha256 line follows the version, the github-release-attachments datasource rewrites it alongside the bump, keeping the checksum control without the manual repin step.
